name: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd
about: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL), a 71.64% Government-owned Maha-Ratna CPSE, designs, manufactures, upgrades and provides lifecycle MRO for aircraft, helicopters, aero -engines, avionics /accessories and aerostructures, principally for India’s armed forces.

flags.text: Operating margin expanded 5.0 pts in 3 years (25% → 30%).
Profit compounding faster than sales (PAT 16.1% vs revenue 7.1% 3y CAGR) — operating leverage.
Operating cash ≥ reported profit over 5 years (1.44x) — earnings are real.

docs.label: May 2026
docs.tone_why: Management addressed execution delays transparently while guiding for solid growth, stable margins, and robust orders.

guidance.statement: Expecting double-digit revenue growth in the range of 10% to 12% minimum for the current financial year.
guidance.quote: it will be in the range of 10% to 12% minimum.

guidance.statement: EBITDA margin will be maintained around 30% to 31% for the current financial year.
guidance.quote: And the EBITDA margin, we have always maintained around 30%, 31%, and it will be maintained.

guidance.statement: Planning to deliver around 20 LCA Mark-1A aircraft during the current financial year.
guidance.quote: So that's why I told 20 LCA we will deliver this year.

guidance.statement: Planning to deliver 20 plus HTT-40 aircraft during the current financial year.
guidance.quote: And we are planning around 20 plus this year to deliver.

guidance.statement: Plan to invest around INR12,000 crores in manufacturing infrastructure and development projects by 2030.
guidance.quote: We plan to invest around INR12,000 crores in these projects by 2030.

pushback.concern: Why are LCA deliveries delayed and is there a risk of spilling beyond FY27?

ar.what_they_do: Manufactures, repairs, overhauls, and develops aircraft, helicopters, aero-engines, and aerospace systems, while providing lifecycle support primarily to the Indian Defence Forces.

segments.name: Aircraft
segments.note: Manufacturing and development of aircraft platforms.

segments.name: Helicopters
segments.note: Developing and producing advanced light and utility helicopters.

segments.name: Repair and Overhaul
segments.note: Servicing and supporting aging and active fleets.

segments.name: Engines and Spares
segments.note: Providing aero-engines, rotables, and essential spare parts.

drivers: Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan and Government policy reforms promoting indigenous defense production.
Strong order book providing 7-8 years of revenue visibility.
Supply chain stabilization, capacity expansion, and faster production ramp-up.

watch.text: Emphasis of matter noting non-compliance with board and committee composition regulations under SEBI and Companies Act.
High Court allowed employees union writ petition regarding workmen pension increment, requiring refund of withheld amounts.
Audit committee was not validly constituted from April 1 to June 1, 2025; RPTs were routed directly to the Board.
Voluntary winding up application filed at NCLT for non-performing joint venture company Infotech HAL Ltd, awaiting final order.
Received stock exchange notices and fines for Listing Regulations non-compliances regarding board composition and delayed filings.

ar.label: Annual Report 2026

verdict.tldr: HAL exhibits strong profitability and cash generation, but persistent execution delays in flagship aircraft programs and a ballooning working capital cycle challenge management's double-digit growth narrative.

promises.promise: Reach double-digit revenue growth of 10% from FY25 onwards.
promises.actual: Reported numbers show Q4 FY25 revenue declined by 7.2% year-on-year.
promises.why: Revenue growth was negative in the target quarter despite guidance.

promises.promise: Maintain EBITDA margins around 26% to 27% in the medium term.
promises.actual: Reported numbers show annual OPM stayed between 30% and 32% for FY24-FY26.
promises.why: Management was overly conservative; actual margins significantly exceeded guidance.

promises.promise: Deliver 16 LCA Mk1A aircraft every year starting from FY25.
promises.actual: T1 admits delays, now targeting 20 deliveries for FY27 instead.
promises.why: Initial delivery schedules were not met due to supply chain issues.

promises.promise: Manufacturing revenue growth expected around 15% to 18% every year.
promises.actual: Reported numbers show a 3-year revenue CAGR of only 7.1%.
promises.why: Realized growth is less than half of the guided manufacturing trajectory.

promises.promise: Invest Rs. 14,000 to Rs. 15,000 crore in capex over five years.
promises.actual: T1 revised the investment plan to INR 12,000 crores by 2030.
promises.why: The total capex target was reduced in subsequent communications.

promises.promise: Bring down manpower cost to 16% of revenue in FY25.
promises.actual: T3 claims 17% achieved in FY24; FY25 specific data missing from reported numbers.
promises.why: Final audited manpower cost ratio for FY25 not explicitly provided.

credibility.line: Management is reliable on margin protection but consistently over-promises on delivery timelines and revenue growth despite a massive order book.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Order book provides 7-8 years of revenue visibility and growth.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Revenue CAGR is only 7.1% over 3 years according to reported numbers.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: EBITDA margins will be maintained around 30% to 31%.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Reported numbers confirm annual OPM of 30% and 31% in FY25-26.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Operating cash flow remains strong and supports growth.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Reported numbers show CFO is 1.44x PAT over 5 years.

bull.point: Strong operating leverage as profits outpace sales growth.
bull.evidence: PAT 3y CAGR of 16.1% vs revenue CAGR of 7.1%.

bull.point: Exceptional cash generation relative to reported earnings.
Robust balance sheet with zero debt and high interest cover.
bull.evidence: Debt/equity is 0.00 with interest cover of 507.3.

bear.point: Significant deterioration in working capital efficiency.
bear.evidence: Cash conversion cycle lengthened from 475 to 788 days.

bear.point: Persistent governance and regulatory compliance issues.
bear.evidence: Fined for non-compliance with board and committee composition regulations.

bear.point: Flagship program delays impacting delivery credibility.
bear.evidence: LCA Mark 1A deliveries pushed back due to supply chain risks.

watch_next: Verification of 20 LCA Mark-1A aircraft deliveries in FY27.
Materialization of the Rs. 1 lakh crore order pipeline within 18 months.
Resolution of board composition non-compliance noted by auditors.
